label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 13 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 133 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 21:25:08 webhook-receiver was recreated on the same image with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, the only recent change. Since then it refuses the provider's webhooks with 'signature mismatch', likely because the provider still signs with the old secret. Refused webhooks are not acknowledged, so the provider resends them and none reach provider-events or the ledger. Unacknowledged webhooks pile up behind the money check's cutoff (133 at the alert, 276 at c8), so the check cannot settle and BooksBehindProvider fires. Open: the tools cannot show which secret the provider signs with, so 'provider on the old secret' and 'receiver's v2 value wrong or missing' cannot be told apart; either way the setting change is the trigger. The HTTP status on refusal was not checked. The remaining queued rate (0.96/s) may be pre-redeploy traffic still in the 2m window. Kafka and consumer lag were not checked.

evidence.shows: The only recent deploy is webhook-receiver at 21:25:08 with settings WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, on the same image (sha256:14898487ce7f). Every other service was deployed at 21:23:41 and has not changed since.
All services are running and healthy with 0 restarts. webhook-receiver alone started later, at 21:25:08, which matches the redeploy. So this is not a crash or an outage of Kafka or the consumers.

result=bad_signature has no points before 21:25:32, then rises from 2.75/s to 13.58/s by 21:26:32. result=queued flattens at about 2.32/s and then falls to 0.96/s. Its 2m rate window still covers traffic from before the redeploy.

webhook-receiver logs 'webhook refused: bad signature' with reason 'signature mismatch' many times a second around 21:26:34, and more_may_exist is true. The level is WARNING, so c3's filter on 'WARN' or 'ERROR' matched none of these lines.
The total webhook rate climbs to 12.8/s by 21:26:27, much faster after 21:25. That fits the provider resending deliveries that were refused and never acknowledged.
A fresh money check could not run: after 20.13 s it had not settled, with 276 webhooks not acknowledged by our receiver. The backlog has grown from the alert's 133.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it ran before the 21:25:08 deploy, so it checks signatures with the secret version the provider was signing with. The provider then retries the refused webhooks and they get acknowledged. Afterwards, confirm that bad_signature drops to 0, that queued rises, and that the money check settles. Move to v2 only once the provider signs with v2, or with the receiver accepting both versions during the rotation.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only webhook-receiver's container is recreated, so it pauses briefly while it restarts. The provider keeps resending unacknowledged webhooks, so no events should be lost. After the rollback a burst of about 276 or more redelivered events reaches provider-events. ledger-consumer runs LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and payment-confirmer runs by_our_id, so duplicates should not double-book, though the burst adds brief load. If the real problem is the provider having moved to v2, the rollback would not help: refusals would continue, but nothing would get worse than now. Nothing was booked wrong; events were only delayed, so no data repair is expected.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If refusals continue or anything else gets worse after the rollback, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, its current setting. Then check with the provider which secret version it signs with, and fix the receiver's v2 secret value instead.
